title: Checkpoint: Hardened Field Parser
prompt: ISO C. A record is `name:score` (name up to 15 chars, score a decimal integer). Implement `int parse_record(const char *line, char *name, size_t namesz, int *score)` — split on the FIRST ':'; copy the name into name only if it fits (NUL included), parse the score with the strictness of strtol (digits only between optional leading +/-; empty or trailing garbage refuses). Return 0 on success; -1 on any refusal (NULL args, no colon, name too long, bad score). Refused outputs are untouched.

tests.name: happy path
tests.hint: world:42 parses cleanly into both outputs.

tests.name: name overflows
tests.hint: A 5-char name does not fit 4 bytes: refusal, score untouched.

tests.name: bad score refuses
tests.hint: exit:3 has no digits after the colon prefix — a refusal, never atoi's silent zero.

tests.name: no colon
tests.hint: A line without a colon is not a record: refuse.
